title: Mosquitto Broker
description: Mosquitto MQTT broker metrics from jryberg/mosquitto-exporter ($SYS topics).

list.name: Broker restart or connection lost
list.titleFormat: Broker restarted or exporter lost the broker

panels.title: Exporter
panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape mosquitto-exporter. If the exporter is up but loses the broker it sets every metric to 0 (--reset-metrics), so an uptime of 0 means the broker connection is down.

targets.expr: min(up{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} and on (job, instance) count_over_time(broker_uptime{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]) > 0)

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: $SYS/broker/uptime. Time since the broker started.

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: $SYS/broker/clients/connected. Clients with an open connection right now.

panels.title: Subscriptions
panels.description: $SYS/broker/subscriptions/count. Active subscriptions on the broker.

panels.title: Msgs in
panels.description: MQTT messages of any type received per second (rate of $SYS/broker/messages/received).

panels.title: Msgs out
panels.description: MQTT messages of any type sent per second (rate of $SYS/broker/messages/sent).

panels.title: Retained
panels.description: $SYS/broker/retained messages/count. Retained messages held by the broker.

panels.title: Dropped
panels.description: PUBLISH messages dropped during the selected time range because a client hit its inflight or queue limit (max_inflight_messages / max_queued_messages). Anything above 0 means subscribers lost messages.

panels.title: Client sessions
panels.description: Connected clients stacked on disconnected persistent sessions (clean session off, still held by the broker). Disconnected is total minus connected, because the disconnected counter published by the broker can wrap around for a moment. The dashed line is the most clients ever connected at once since the broker started.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Share of known client sessions that are connected right now versus disconnected persistent sessions.

panels.title: New socket connections
panels.description: Rate of $SYS/broker/connections/socket/count: TCP connections opened to the broker per second, whether or not the MQTT login succeeded. A steady high rate with few connected clients points at clients stuck in a reconnect loop, for example with bad credentials.

panels.title: Subscriptions
panels.description: Active subscriptions ($SYS/broker/subscriptions/count) and shared subscriptions ($SYS/broker/shared_subscriptions/count).

panels.title: Expired sessions
panels.description: Disconnected persistent sessions removed by persistent_client_expiration, per interval (increase of $SYS/broker/clients/expired).

panels.title: Messages
panels.description: MQTT messages of every type (CONNECT, PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE, PINGREQ, acks, …) per second. Sent is drawn above zero and received below.

panels.title: Bytes
panels.description: All bytes on the wire per second, including protocol overhead. Sent is drawn above zero and received below.

panels.title: PUBLISH messages
panels.description: PUBLISH messages per second, the application traffic. Sent is usually higher than received because one message fans out to every matching subscriber.

panels.title: PUBLISH payload bytes
panels.description: Payload bytes carried by PUBLISH messages per second.

panels.title: Dropped PUBLISH messages
panels.description: PUBLISH messages dropped per interval because a client hit its inflight or queue limit. Should stay empty.

panels.title: Average PUBLISH payload size
panels.description: PUBLISH payload bytes divided by PUBLISH messages. A shift shows that the kind of traffic changed.

panels.title: Payload share of traffic
panels.description: PUBLISH payload bytes as a share of all bytes. The rest is protocol overhead: headers, topics, acks, keepalives and connection handshakes.

panels.title: Messages received
panels.description: Messages received per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: Messages sent
panels.description: Messages sent per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: Connections opened
panels.description: Connections opened per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: PUBLISH received
panels.description: PUBLISH received per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: PUBLISH sent
panels.description: PUBLISH sent per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: PUBLISH dropped
panels.description: PUBLISH dropped per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: Bytes received per minute
panels.description: Bytes received per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: Bytes sent per minute
panels.description: Bytes sent per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: Sockets opened
panels.description: Sockets opened per minute as a moving average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, computed by the broker itself ($SYS/broker/load/…). Read it like a Unix load average: 1 min above 15 min means the load is rising.

panels.title: Broker heap memory
panels.description: Heap memory used by the broker ($SYS/broker/heap/current) and the largest it has been since start (dashed). Only published when the broker is built with memory tracking.

panels.title: Stored messages
panels.description: $SYS/broker/store/messages/count. Messages held in the message store: retained messages and messages queued for persistent clients.

panels.title: Message store size
panels.description: $SYS/broker/store/messages/bytes. Payload bytes held in the message store.

panels.title: Outgoing packet queue
panels.description: $SYS/broker/packet/out/count. Packets waiting to be written to client sockets. Growth means clients or the network cannot keep up.

panels.title: Outgoing packet queue size
panels.description: $SYS/broker/packet/out/bytes. Bytes waiting to be written to client sockets.

panels.title: Memory (RSS)
panels.description: Resident memory of the mosquitto-exporter process.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by the mosquitto-exporter process, in cores.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines in the mosquitto-exporter process.

targets.expr: sum(go_goroutines{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} and on (job, instance) count_over_time(broker_uptime{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]) > 0)

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: File descriptors held by the mosquitto-exporter process.

targets.expr: sum(process_open_fds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} and on (job, instance) count_over_time(broker_uptime{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]) > 0)

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: How long Prometheus takes to scrape the exporter.

targets.expr: max(scrape_duration_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} and on (job, instance) count_over_time(broker_uptime{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]) > 0)

panels.title: Samples per scrape
panels.description: Samples returned per scrape. A drop means the exporter lost its $SYS subscription.

targets.expr: sum(scrape_samples_scraped{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} and on (job, instance) count_over_time(broker_uptime{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]) > 0)
